## Findings
- claim-1: For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the source states that \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1354-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: Under the explicit box-Schur realization \(I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), the requested restriction \(J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1}\) and its descent to indecomposables are established for every \(i,j,p,c\ge1\).
## Strategy
Assume the box-Schur realization, for \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathbb Zs_\lambda\),
\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda ,
\qquad
\Lambda/I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda .
\]
Let \(i,j,p,c\ge1\), \(q=i+p\), \(r=j+c\), and
\[
J_{p,c}:=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\subseteq\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}.
\]
Using the source-backed generating set and the Littlewood–Richardson containment
\(c_{\mu,\nu}^{\lambda}\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\subseteq\lambda\), one obtains the Schur-basis formula
\[
J_{p,c}
=
\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, every displayed \(\bar s_\lambda\) is among the given ideal generators; conversely, multiplication of a generator indexed by \(\mu\supseteq i^j\) has only Schur terms indexed by \(\lambda\supseteq\mu\supseteq i^j\), with terms outside \((i+p)^{j+c}\) zero.

Since \(p,c\ge1\),
\[
(i+1)^{j+1}\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c},
\]
so \(I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1}\), yielding
\[
\pi:\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}\twoheadrightarrow\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
Basiswise, for every \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}\),
\[
\pi(\bar s_\lambda)=
\begin{cases}
\bar s_\lambda,&\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},\\
0,&\lambda\not\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}.
\end{cases} \tag{2}
\]
Thus every class outside the smaller rectangle maps to \(0\), while every retained class lies in
\[
J_{1,1}
=
\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda.
\]
Equation (2) maps onto every basis element of \(J_{1,1}\); hence
\[
\pi|_{J_{p,c}}:J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1}.
\]
For \(\Lambda_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}\Lambda_d\), \(\Lambda\)-linearity gives
\[
\pi(\Lambda_+J_{p,c})
=\Lambda_+\pi(J_{p,c})
=\Lambda_+J_{1,1}.
\]
Therefore it descends surjectively to
\[
J_{p,c}/\Lambda_+J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow
J_{1,1}/\Lambda_+J_{1,1}.
\]
For \(p=c=1\), \(\pi\) is the identity map and the same statements hold.

## Gaps
The supplied source excerpt establishes the ideal-generating set, but does not ground the required box-Schur realization of \(I_{r,q}\). Therefore this certificate is established only conditional on that realization, not unconditionally.

\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda
\]
and the corresponding surviving Schur basis of \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\).
